evidence.claim: A queued slashing reverts in finalizeSlashing when a vault's totalAssets has dropped to zero (via a completed withdrawal or a prior 100% slash), because Vault.slashAssets forwards transferAmount==0 to SlashingHandler.handleSlashing which reverts with ZeroAmount, blocking slashing of all other vaults in the same request.
evidence.support_reason: Vault.slashAssets (Vault.sol:198) computes transferAmount = Math.min(totalAssets(), totalAssetsToSlash) with no zero guard, then unconditionally calls handleSlashing (Vault.sol:202). SlashingHandler.handleSlashing reverts on amount==0 (SlashingHandler.sol:53). SlasherLib.finalizeSlashing (SlasherLib.sol:134-139) loops over all vaults with no try/catch, so one zero-asset vault reverts the whole finalize. Nothing removes a vault from the DSS stake set on withdrawal (Operator.sol:103-109 only changes on requestUpdateVaultStakeInDSS), so the empty vault stays in the slashing set.
preconditions: A vault in the queued slashing request has totalAssets()==0 at finalize time (full withdrawal completed, or prior 100% slash by another DSS).
The vault is still staked to the DSS (no unstake finalized), which is the default since withdrawals don't touch stake state.

missing_evidence.item: Demonstration that the zero-asset vault remains in the DSS stake set at finalize time (i.e., that a completed withdrawal does not remove it), since the report's own PoC relies on this and the code path (Operator.sol:103-109) only updates on requestUpdateVaultStakeInDSS.
missing_evidence.why: Reachability of the revert depends on the empty vault still being in queuedSlashing.vaults; if withdrawals removed it, the loop would never hit the zero-asset vault. The report asserts this but the provided test is unverified; a judge needs the actual state check confirmed against the audited code.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: A runnable test (or trace) shows fetchVaultsStakedInDSS still contains the emptied vault after finishRedeem, and finalizeSlashing reverts with ZeroAmount.

missing_evidence.item: Clarification of whether the DoS is a genuine protocol-level griefing vector or an expected consequence of the documented 'DSS should stop considering queued withdrawals' policy, i.e., whether the DSS is expected to re-request slashing excluding the empty vault.
missing_evidence.why: The contest policy states DSS should stop considering vaults with queued withdrawals for rewards/weight; if the intended design is that DSS re-issues slashing requests, the 'blocked slashing' impact may be an accepted operational cost rather than a bug. This is a policy ambiguity the claim depends on.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: The policy or sponsor statement confirms that a single zero-asset vault reverting the entire finalizeSlashing (including healthy vaults) is not an accepted design outcome.

missing_evidence.item: Confirmation that the revert is not merely a transient/retryable condition with no lasting harm (anyone can re-request after the empty vault is unstaked), which affects severity.
missing_evidence.why: The report itself notes the operator can re-request; this bears on whether impact is High/Medium/Low but does not undermine the existence of the revert path.
missing_evidence.resolves_when: Severity is argued against the actual re-request cost (2-day veto window, possible further withdrawals).
